title: City of Los Angeles Ordinance No. 188797 (2026 L.A. amendments to 2025 California codes) - electrical (LAMC Ch. IX Art. 3) excerpt
effectiveDate: effective upon publication (passed 2025-12-12, approved 2025-12-24; exact publication date not stated)
keyFacts: Ordinance amends LAMC Chapter IX to incorporate portions of the 2025 California Building Standards Code (ord. p.1).
LAMC 93.0101: Article 3 is the 'Los Angeles Electrical Code'; 'CEC' means the 2025 California Electrical Code (ord. p.105-106, Sec. 511).
LAMC 93.0700: adopts Chapters 1-9 and Annexes C, H, G and I of the 2023 NEC plus the CEC by reference; LAMC prevails per 93.0105 on conflict (ord. p.111, Sec. 518).

LAMC 93.0202(a) permit exemptions include: like-for-like repair/replacement of fixed motors/appliances on branch circuits <=20 A and <=240 V (not in Art. 500 hazardous areas); festive lighting in dwellings <=90 days; replacing an overcurrent device of same rating/location; reinstalling attachment-plug receptacles (not outlets); like-in-kind luminaire replacement in single-family dwellings (ord. p.106-107, Sec. 512).

Low-voltage exemption (93.0202(a)13) covers non-required Class 2 signaling <=30 V/100 VA and circuits <=12.4 V/25 W, but NOT in hazardous locations, fire alarm (Art. 760), fire-resistive penetrations, or plenums/air-handling spaces (ord. p.107).
Smoke/CO alarm replacement in single-family dwellings by a contractor with a Certificate of Registration (LAMC 91.1704) needs a Certificate of Compliance in lieu of a permit (ord. p.108).

LAMC 93.0206(b): electrical plan check required before permit for theaters, assembly, Art. 517 health care, buildings/additions >30,000 sq ft, first-time tenants, new total connected load >400 A or equipment rated >=600 A, >600 V, hazardous locations, exit/egress lighting, emergency/standby/fire alarm/gas detection, luminaires >300 lb, PV/ESS (except approved online standard plans) (ord. p.108-109, Sec. 513).

LAMC 93.0501: only a 'qualified installer' (CA contractor license in classification, LADBS Maintenance Certificate of Registration, qualifying owner-occupant of single-family dwelling, qualified government employee, or journey-level person per CSLB who cannot contract jobs requiring a permit or >$1,000) may do electrical work, or work under their direct supervision (ord. p.110-111, Sec. 517).

LAMC 93.0700.19: illuminated exit signs in an emergency system must be fed from two independent branch circuits (one emergency, one normal), except battery-equipped emergency luminaires per CEC 700.12(H) (ord. p.112, Sec. 519).
LAMC 93.0402: equipment must be LADBS-approved, listed, or certified by an LADBS-approved testing agency; test labs must be on the OSHA (NRTL) list (ord. p.110, Sec. 516).
Urgency clause: ordinance effective upon publication to align with Title 24 effective 2026-01-01 (ord. p.162, Sec. 633); passed 2025-12-12, approved by Mayor 2025-12-24 (ord. p.164).
notes: Full ordinance is 44.9 MB / 164 pp (all trades); only pp. 1-3, 105-112, 162-164 saved. Page numbers in keyFacts are the ordinance's printed page numbers. Unchanged Article 3 sections (e.g., 93.0201 permit required, inspections) are not in this ordinance; see lamc-ch9-art3-amlegal entry.

title: LADBS Inspection (how it works, requesting, cancelling)
keyFacts: Must call for inspection before covering or concealing any work; work is not approved until inspected and accepted (How it works).
Work is inspected in succession; no work may proceed past each inspection point without inspector approval; final inspection required (About Inspections).
Request inspections online or by 311, or (213) 473-3231 outside L.A. (Requesting an Inspection).
Have the permit, approved plans (if plan review was required), and access equipment such as a ladder on site (During the Inspection).
Virtual, off-hour and Saturday inspections can be requested (page links).

title: DIR/DLSE Electrician Certification Program home
publisher: California Dept. of Industrial Relations, Labor Commissioner (DLSE) Electrician Certification Unit
keyFacts: Persons performing work as electricians for a C-10 licensed contractor must be certified per Labor Code 108 (page body).
New exam scheduling procedures for exams on/after 2026-06-01, administered by CPS HR Consulting (notice).
Applications for certification, renewal and retest are online; trainee registration still by mail (notice).

title: DIR Electrician Certification FAQ
keyFacts: Out-of-state electricians must be certified before working in California; no grace period, even for a short single job (Who is required to be certified).
An electrician license from another state makes you eligible to sit for the exam, but you must still test and certify; no reciprocity (Who is required).

Certification applies to connections >100 VA for C-10 contractors; not required for C-7 low-voltage or C-45 sign work within scope, or for employees of school districts/plants (Labor Code 108, 108.2).
The C-10 qualifying person need not be certified; non-qualifying partners/officers must be (LC 108.2(g)).
Five classifications: General Electrician; Residential Electrician; Fire/Life Safety; Voice Data Video; Non-residential Lighting Technician (certification section).
General exam: 100 questions/4 hours; open book, computer-based, multiple choice, based on NEC; 70% to pass; 60-day wait to retest (test section).
Certification valid 3 years; renewal requires 32 hours CE from approved provider plus 2,000 hours industry work, $100 (renewal section).
Insufficient hours: register as electrician trainee with enrollment in a state-approved school (certification section).

title: DIR Electrician certification categories and eligibility
keyFacts: On-the-job experience to sit for exam: General Electrician 8,000 h; Residential 4,800 h; Fire/Life/Safety 4,000 h; Voice/Data/Video 4,000 h; Non-residential Lighting 2,000 h (table).
Paths also exist for registered apprentices and trainees without enough experience (table).

title: CSLB C-10 Electrical Contractor classification
keyFacts: C-10 contractor places, installs, erects or connects electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, raceways, conduits, solar PV cells or any part thereof (16 CCR Div. 8 Art. 3).

title: CSLB Steps to Becoming a Licensed Contractor (13P-103/1025)
keyFacts: Projects >= $1,000 labor+materials, or needing a permit or workers, require a CSLB license (p.1).
Qualifying individual: 18+, at least 4 years journey-level experience in the classification within the last 10 years (Step 1).
$450 application fee; fingerprinting; law and trade exams unless waived (Steps 3-6).

title: CSLB General Information on Reciprocity
keyFacts: California has contractor reciprocity agreements with Arizona, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada and North Carolina (B&P Code 7065.4) (page body).

title: CSLB Reciprocity Requirements
keyFacts: Must have held an active license in good standing in the reciprocal state for the previous 5 years, in a class on the Reciprocal Classifications List (page body).
Requires Request for Verification of License from the other state plus Application for Original Contractor's License (page body).

title: CSLB Reciprocity Exam Requirements
keyFacts: Reciprocity may waive the trade exam, but CSLB may still require it; the business law exam is always required (page body).

title: LADWP Electric Service Requirements (ESR) Manual, 2025 Edition (2025-11-18)
publisher: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
keyFacts: 2025 Edition dated 2025-11-18; electronic distribution only; subject to periodic revision (p.1 Notice).
Sections: service/metering 0-600 V, LV switchboards, MV switchgear 601-34,500 V, conduit on private property, overhead services, parallel generation/ESS (Contents p.i).
LADWP energizes service only after inspection and clearance by both LADWP and the permitting agency (Sec. 1 B.6.a, p.1-8).
Customer obtains electrical permit; permitting agency final electrical release must reach LADWP, which can take several days (Sec. 1 B.6.b, p.1-8).
Temporary service also requires permitting-agency inspection and final release before energizing; decorative/carnival temporary power generally limited to 90 days (temporary service section).
notes: LADWP is a City of Los Angeles department (public). Manual includes EUSERC drawings; treat drawings with care if redistributing.
